Result: word bit1 (usefulCnt.value) of the alt entry is written with a value that is not derived from the stored bit (DontCare lowered to 0 or folded to some other operand by firtool), while bit0 (paddingBit, itself DontCare at IttageTable.scala:260) is the only bit preserved.
reason: The requirement is that a write with usefulCntValid=0 leaves the stored usefulCnt.value bit unchanged. On the alt-provider path the table receives update.valid=1 with usefulCntValid=0, selects updateNoUsBitmask, and that mask has bit 1 set because paddingBit occupies bit 0 and usefulCnt sits at bit 1; the SRAM does a per-bit masked write with no read-modify-write, so the alt entry's useful bit is overwritten with the lowered DontCare value of updateUsefulCnt(altProvider). No other mechanism restores it: IttageMeta carries only providerUsefulCnt (Bundles.scala:68), not the alt provider's useful bit, so no path can reconstruct the stored value, and the tick-driven reset sweep uses updateUsBitmask = bit 0 only, which touches paddingBit rather than usefulCnt. Whatever constant or operand firtool substitutes for the DontCare, it is independent of SRAM contents, so a stored useful=1 alt entry is not guaranteed to stay 1 (with the default lowering of invalid to 0 it is cleared on every alt-provider mispredict update). The wrong result violates the requirement.

UsefulCntWidth=1 and the field order are fixed by the active parameters, so nothing constant-folds the path away.
